newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open lower but retrace loss.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open lower but retrace loss.

text.p: French stocks opened weaker on Thursday but quickly retraced their fall to trade slightly higher, helped by a modest rise in the German Ifo business sentiment index for August.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 1.59 points, or 0.08 percent, at 2,074.32 at 0845 GMT after opening at 2,067.73. The CAC September futures contract was up 3.5 points at 2,079.
Volume was a modest 300 million francs.
Retailer Pinault-Printemps-Redoute was the top gainer on the CAC, rising more than three percent after reporting a jump in first-half profit on Wednesday. The stock rose 48 francs at 1,869.

It said first-half net attributable profit rose to 748 million francs from 452 million, but cautioned that it saw no spending pick-up and that full-year results could not be extrapolated from the first-half increase.
Insurance group Assurances Generales de France (AGF) dipped after reporting a strong first-half profit rise. The share had risen sharply ahead of the results.

Holding group Cie de Suez, up 1.41 percent, is about to receive offers for a huge property portfolio but bids from suitors are likely to be far below the net portfolio value of 11 billion francs, L'Agefi newspaper said on Thursday.

French property financing group UIC, which is controlled by state-owned insurer GAN, was suspended limit down. It had been suspended for the entire day at 45 francs on Wednesday after falling 10.30 francs or 18.6 percent.
UIC said the preceding day its share was considerably overvalued on the basis of its negative net asset value.
